evidence.quote: If Family Income of a patient not enrolled in Medicaid is less than or equal to 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, the patient will receive 100% charity care adjustment for Eligible Health Care Services (consistent with Indigent Care Trust Fund requirements).

tiers.description: Uninsured patients not enrolled in Medicaid receive 100% financial assistance for the patient's personal responsibility for Eligible Health Care Services. Charges are limited to AGB. Insured patients in this band are not clearly covered.

evidence.quote: If Family Income of a patient who is not enrolled in Medicaid and is uninsured is at least 201% but less than or equal to 350% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, the patient will receive 100% financial assistance for the patient’s personal responsibility for Eligible Health Care Services.

presumptive_eligibility: Medicaid beneficiaries are deemed presumptively eligible for 100% assistance on Medicaid non-covered charges, and an External Screening Process using public records can presumptively determine eligibility.
how_to_apply: Apply electronically through MyChart, at the hospital Patient Access Office (Appendix C), or by mail to Emory Healthcare, P.O. Box 746699, Atlanta, GA 30374-6699. Telephone: (404) 778-7318.
warnings: The 201%-350% FPL band applies only to uninsured patients not enrolled in Medicaid. Insured patients are eligible for the up-to-200% free care band, and possibly for the Catastrophic Care Adjustment.
Free care at or below 200% FPL applies to patients not enrolled in Medicaid; Medicaid patients are covered for non-covered charges.
Patients above 350% FPL may get a 65% self-pay discount, which is explicitly not financial assistance under the policy.
A Catastrophic Care Adjustment is available above 225% FPL, case by case, capping the balance at 20% of annual Family Income.

Asset consideration is not addressed in policy rules, though the application form lists savings and checking accounts as income types and requests bank statements; bank statements are used for income verification.
The application form says approvals are valid for a maximum of 6 months while the policy says 12 months.
Application deadline is the later of 240 days after the first post-discharge billing statement or 30 days after written notice of intent to initiate extraordinary collection actions.
Policy covers multiple Emory hospitals in Georgia; the same rules appear to apply to all.
Policy mentions Temporary Visitor in the definitions but no residency requirement is stated in the rules.
